page: Amazon Web Services m6g.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the 64-core AWS Graviton2 processor built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz. Each virtual CPU corresponds directly to a dedicated physical core with one thread per core, avoiding simultaneous multithreading resource contention. The system provides 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The instance operates under the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, and provisions zero local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing scalability alongside distinct single-thread architectural limits. In multi-threaded execution, the instance achieves top-tier scores in stress-ng multi-core compute tests and Clang software compilation benchmarks, reflecting effective 64-core throughput. In memory-intensive services, the instance registers strong outcomes with 72.59 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 45.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core metrics sit in lower distribution bands, including weak single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core processing.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the Graviton2 ARM architecture, offering high compute concurrency per resource allocation compared to legacy x86 equivalents. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means sustained disk I/O requires network storage, and vector-intensive extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are absent. The instance is primarily suited for multi-threaded enterprise application servers, large-scale container clusters, in-memory caches, software build infrastructure, and microservices fleets.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 64-core AWS Graviton2 processor running on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it features 256.0 GB of RAM, a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, zero local storage, and runs under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmarks reveal strong parallel performance, achieving high throughput in multi-core compute stress tests, Clang compilation, and Redis operations yielding 72.59 million operations per second. While single-thread decompression and Geekbench single-core metrics fall into lower performance quartiles, the instance provides high compute density across balanced memory allocations. It is well suited for container orchestration fleets, multi-threaded application servers, in-memory caching systems, and distributed CI/CD build environments.
